{{Quote|In the name of the Emperor, I claim this planet as Imperial territory.|An Imperial officer on Gibbela|<ref name="Tales19" />}}
The '''Gibbela system''' was a part of the [[Atrivis sector/Legends|Atrivis sector]] in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA" /> It was located far from even minor [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] and contained the isolated terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Gibbela]].<ref name="Tales19" /> Gibbela was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifter]] [[Dazouri]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="Shapeshifters" /> When provoked, the Dazouri would transform from their normal non-threatening [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]] form into three-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]-tall homicidal and frenzied<ref name="Planets">''[[The Star Wars Planets Collection]]''</ref> [[Diet/Legends|predators]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|340|Gibbela}}</ref> As a result, [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] tended to avoid visiting Gibbela.<ref name="Tales19" />

During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], that government made plans to [[Colonist/Legends|colonize]] Gibbela. An Imperial [[Scout/Legends|scout]] detachment,<ref name="CSWE" /> consisting of a [[Sentinel-class landing craft/Legends|''Sentinel''-class landing craft]] carrying an [[Unidentified Imperial officer (Gibbela)|Imperial officer]] and a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] escort,<ref name="Tales19" /> was [[Mission to Gibbela|dispatched]] to the planet.<ref name="CSWE" /> However, when the [[Landing craft/Legends|starship]] landed at the [[Unidentified farm (Gibbela)|farm]] of [[Unidentified Dazouri farmer|one]] of the Dazouri and the [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer]] claimed Gibbela as [[Imperial Space|Imperial territory]] and demanded the [[Farmer/Legends|farmer's]] surrender, the Dazouri underwent<ref name="Tales19" /> their species' characteristic<ref name="Shapeshifters" /> transformation and wiped out the Imperial force.<ref name="Tales19" /> Between [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], the Gibbela [[Star system/Legends|system]] fell within the [[Pentastar Alignment]]'s borders.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Gibbela system was introduced via an appearance of Gibbela in "[[The Value of Proper Intelligence to Any Successful Military Campaign is Not to Be Underestimated]]," a [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] story written by [[Ken Lizzl]], illustrated by [[Lucas Marangon]], and published in the [[Star Wars Tales 19|nineteenth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' comic-book series<ref name="Tales19" /> on [[May 14]], [[2004]].<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53997/star_wars_tales_1999_19|text=Star Wars Tales (1999) #19}}</ref> With respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, [[Lucasfilm]] considered plausible stories in [[Star Wars Tales 1|''Star Wars Tales'' 1]]&ndash;[[Star Wars Tales 20|20]] to be [[Canon|S-canon]],<ref name="Tales1-20">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=752#14952461|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-06-04|time=3:05 AM|quote=Consider everything that's not completely outrageous or intentionally comic as S-canon. If it's referenced in another non-''Tales'' source, then elevate it to C-canon.}}</ref> or "secondary" canon,<ref name="Canon">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?forumID=24&start=15&threadID=152583&msRange=15#5706120|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2004-01-21|time=9:16 AM}}</ref> by default until they were referenced in a non-''Tales'' source, at which point the subject matter was elevated to C-canon,<ref name="Tales1-20" /> or "continuity" canon.<ref name="Canon" />

The events of the comic story from ''Star Wars Tales'' 19 were later mentioned in an entry for Gibbela in the [[2008]] ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CSWE" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], named the Gibbela system and placed it in grid square L-5.<ref name="TEA" />
